quickSummary: The frog nervous system includes CNS (brain and spinal cord), PNS (10 pairs of cranial nerves and 10 pairs of spinal nerves), and ANS. The brain has a forebrain (olfactory lobes, cerebral hemispheres, diencephalon), midbrain (optic lobes), and hindbrain (reduced cerebellum, medulla oblongata). Amphibians have strictly 10 pairs of cranial nerves (XI and XII absent). Hearing relies on a tympanum and a single middle ear ossicle (Columella auris).

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Frogs have strictly 10 pairs of cranial nerves (XI and XII absent). Middle ear has a single ossicle (Columella auris). Cerebellum is poorly developed.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
FROG BRAIN DIVISIONS
                                     │
     ┌───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┐
     ▼                               ▼                               ▼
FOREBRAIN (Prosencephalon)      MIDBRAIN (Mesencephalon)       HINDBRAIN (Rhombencephalon)
├── Olfactory Lobes (Smell)     └── Pair of prominent          ├── Cerebellum (Poorly developed)
├── Cerebral Hemispheres (Voluntary) OPTIC LOBES (Vision)      └── Medulla Oblongata
└── Diencephalon (Epiphysis/Pituitary)                             (Passes via Foramen Magnum)
conceptBreakdown.content:
The central nervous system comprises the brain enclosed in the cranium and the spinal cord protected in the vertebral column.

### Brain Regions
1. **Forebrain (Prosencephalon)**: Olfactory lobes (smell), Cerebral hemispheres (voluntary coordination), and Diencephalon (bears pineal body/epiphysis and pituitary/hypophysis; encloses 3rd ventricle).
2. **Midbrain (Mesencephalon)**: Pair of large, spherical **Optic Lobes** (vision).
3. **Hindbrain (Rhombencephalon)**: Reduced narrow **Cerebellum** (reflecting basic motor coordination) and **Medulla Oblongata** (enclosing 4th ventricle, exiting cranium via the Foramen Magnum).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.1 The 10 Pairs of Amphibian Cranial Nerves
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.1 The 10 Pairs of Amphibian Cranial Nerves
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
FROG CRANIAL NERVE SUMMARY
                           
   I. Olfactory (Sensory)    ──► Nasal Epithelium (Smell)
  II. Optic (Sensory)        ──► Retina of Eye (Vision)
 III. Oculomotor (Motor)     ──► Eye Muscles (Movement)
  IV. Trochlear (Motor)      ──► Superior Oblique Eye Muscle
   V. Trigeminal (Mixed)     ──► Snout, Jaws, & Face (Largest nerve)
  VI. Abducens (Motor)       ──► Lateral Rectus Eye Muscle
 VII. Facial (Mixed)         ──► Face, Hyoid, & Tongue
VIII. Vestibulocochlear (Sensory) ──► Internal Ear (Auditory/Balance)
  IX. Glossopharyngeal (Mixed)──► Tongue & Pharynx
   X. Vagus (Mixed)          ──► Lungs, Heart, Stomach, & Viscera
conceptBreakdown.content: Frogs possess **strictly 10 pairs of cranial nerves** (*Amniotes—reptiles, birds, and mammals—possess 12 pairs, having evolved XI Spinal Accessory and XII Hypoglossal*).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.2 Sense Organs & Auditory Mechanics
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.2 Sense Organs & Auditory Mechanics
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Visual Apparatus**: Bulged lateral eyes with spherical non-deformable lenses; accommodation is performed by shifting the lens using the **Protractor Lentis** muscle.
• **Auditory & Equilibrium Apparatus**:
  - External ear/pinna is ABSENT.
  - **Middle Ear**: Consists of the superficial circular **Tympanum** and a single slender middle ear bone called the **Columella Auris** (homologous to the mammalian stapes), which conducts sound waves to the inner ear.
  - **Internal Ear (Labyrinth)**: Fluid-filled chamber with statoliths maintaining static and dynamic equilibrium.
